name: Kawacha
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Lloyd, R.G. 1973 (Angan subclassification, p.36) named; no grammar or phonology of Kawacha located

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1973. Appendices (Appendix A: Angan, A.8 Kawacha). In Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 539-592. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU (full volume, hdl 1885/145149)
sources.note: App. A.8 Kawacha, p. 549: Swadesh-100 word list (1. kwoyava/kwe.. 100. panewio) in narrow transcription, apostrophe = glottal stop; no stress or tone marks on any item; appendix introduction (p. 541) gives no prosodic transcription conventions.
sources.venue: The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kawa1276 and langdoc listing
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Lloyd 1973 (phonology or text collection), Fischer 1968 (a wordlist or less); no grammar, phonology or dictionary of Kawacha exists in the bibliography (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. Kawacha Swadesh List (kcb). archive.org item rosettaproject_kcb_swadesh-1
sources.note: Same 100 items as Franklin 1973 App. A.8 (source not stated); no stress marking (one stray acute in 'that: to´nïnu' corresponds to the glottal stop in Lloyd's to'nɨnu).
Stub: nearly extinct, ~12 speakers, Katsiong village, Tsewi ward, Kome Rural LLG; no phonology.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38
sources.note: Kawacha appears only in the Angan speaker table ('Kawacha 30'); nothing on phonology or stress.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study 1

sources.citation: Lloyd, Richard G. 1973. The Angan language family. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 31-110. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C26.31
sources.note: Sec. 2.11 Kawacha (p. 79): ~30 speakers at Karunja hamlet, Katsiong; only survey word lists collected. Sec. 2.111 Phonology (pp. 79-80): consonants p t k ' f m n ng s l r w y (h likely), vowels i ɨ u e a o aa, allophony, syllabic nasals, clusters, vowel sequences; NOTHING on stress, tone or accent for Kawacha. p. 36: Kawacha forms 'remain in a narrower transcription' because 'only word lists are available'.
